name: Context Memory Harness
summary: A local memory shared by AI assistants: every coding session, chat, codebase and document goes into one store on the owner's laptop, and assistants on any machine retrieve from it with sources attached.

stages.title: Sources
stages.what: Claude Code sessions from every machine (pushed by a session hook over SSH), claude.ai and Perplexity conversations (read back through a logged-in local browser), codebases (git-tracked files) and Markdown documentation.

stages.title: Ingress checks
stages.what: A secret scanner rejects documents that contain credentials (chat logs are redacted instead), and only folders the owner listed can be read.

stages.title: Chunking
stages.what: Markdown is split at headings; Python at classes and methods, keeping line ranges so every chunk points back to exact lines; other text in token-bounded blocks.

stages.title: Embedding
stages.what: Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B at a pinned revision, float32 on a 6 GB consumer GPU (GTX 1660 Ti), fully offline after the first download. float16 measured slower on this card.

stages.title: Storage
stages.what: SQLite holds metadata, provenance, a full-text index and a hash-chained audit log; LanceDB holds the vectors. A changed source retires old chunks instead of deleting them, so history survives.

stages.title: Knowledge graph
stages.what: Projects, documents, modules, classes, methods and imports, extracted from the stored chunks. Every edge cites the chunk it came from and expires when that chunk is retired.

stages.title: Retrieval
stages.what: Vector search, BM25 full-text search, or both fused by reciprocal rank fusion (k = 60). On the owner's corpus (about 12,000 chunks, 30 queries) hybrid found the right document in the top 5 for 0.90 of queries [95% CI 0.80 to 0.98] against 0.75 [0.58 to 0.90] for vector alone; warm hybrid search takes about 150 ms locally.

citation.text: Gordon V. Cormack, Charles L A Clarke, Stefan Buettcher (2009). Reciprocal rank fusion outperforms condorcet and individual rank learning methods. Proceedings of the 32nd international ACM SIGIR conference on Research and development in information retrieval

stages.title: Verification
stages.what: Results that come from local files are re-checked against the file at query time and labelled verified, stale or missing; chat excerpts stay unverified.

stages.title: Disclosure Gate
stages.what: Before anything leaves the memory, a deterministic gate withholds attribute types (contact details, precise location, financial and credential data) according to who receives it: the owner, a local model, a cloud model, or the public.

stages.title: Delivery
stages.what: Claude Code on any machine receives a short context pack when a session starts and can search the memory over MCP; remote machines reach it only through SSH. The owner has a private console; visitors get this site, served from an exported public copy.

gate.returns: what each recipient class would receive
